documents: Telloli et al. 2022, Adv. Geosci. 57, 21–36, published PDF

entry.evidence: Although the Treviso plain has been extensively investigated, its hydro-structure is not perfectly defined

sequences.source_document: g22_W4220711460.xml.txt (publisher XML), checked against the published PDF

steps.action: Take the expected tritium content of local precipitation (5–6 TU, up to 7 TU with mountain contributions) from the Cauquoin et al. (2015) atmospheric model.
steps.quote: the precipitations in the sampling area have on average concentrations of tritium with maximum values of 5–6 TU

steps.action: Take the seasonal cycle of rainfall tritium (about 4 TU in January, peaks of 9.5 TU) from the GNIP Locarno station record, 2000–2009.
steps.quote: it is also possible to observe a seasonal variability of the content of tritium in rainwater

steps.action: State the interpretive rule taken from the literature: aquifer tritium close to atmospheric levels means recent recharge, and lower values mean slow or no meteoric recharge.
steps.quote: the more the concentrations of tritium are similar or equal to atmospheric ones, the more recent the recharge of the aquifer is

steps.action: Pose the problem that the hydro-structure and recharge dynamics of the Treviso multi-aquifer system are poorly defined, and set the aim of verifying aquifer vulnerability.
steps.quote: its hydro-structure is not perfectly defined

steps.action: Design a combined tracer survey: tritium plus stable isotopes (18O, 2H) and hydrochemistry, to identify water origin and possible anthropogenic pollution in relation to tritium.
steps.quote: we tested the reliability of water stable isotopes, in addition to hydrochemical parameters

steps.action: In May 2018, sample 31 private artesian wells over about 50 km2. Measure tritium by distillation, electrolytic enrichment (260 mL to 10 mL) and low-level LSC (Quantulus), stable isotopes by CRDS, and major ions by APHA methods.
steps.quote: each sample was subjected to an electrolytic enrichment process prior to measurement

steps.action: Calibrate the tritium LSC spectra against reference standards and report 1σ analytical errors of ±0.31 to ±1.01 TU (mean 0.5 TU).
steps.quote: The spectrum obtained is then interpreted thanks to the comparison with reference standards

steps.action: Compute the local meteoric water line and adopt the GMWL as the reference where waters of meteoric origin are expected to plot.
steps.quote: In this research paper we calculate the local meteoric water lines (LMWL)

steps.action: Classify the samples into five tritium classes with inferred recharge ages (tritium-free >70 yr; <0.8 TU 50–70 yr; 0.8–5 TU 10–50 yr; 5–7 TU 1–10 yr; >7 TU possible contamination), while noting the piston-flow assumption.
steps.quote: The samples are classified in five categories

steps.action: Plot tritium against δ18O and δD. Casier samples are isotopically depleted, Preganziol samples cluster, and no significant pattern appears elsewhere.
steps.quote: tritium values are correlated with the results obtained for stable isotopes

steps.action: Describe the physico-chemical parameters: uniform T and pH, conductivity 362–663 µS/cm (lower in Casier), DO 1.6–6.2 mg/L, Eh both negative and positive without a site pattern.
steps.quote: Temperature and pH value are generally the same in all the samples analysed

steps.action: Correlate well depth with CE, Eh and tritium, and tritium with SO4, Cl, Mg/Ca and Na. No correlations emerge, except one high-tritium, high-sulphate Casier well.
steps.quote: No correlation was also observed between the depth of the wells and the tritium value

steps.action: Plot major ions on a Piper diagram. Preganziol samples are homogeneous; Casier splits into two groups; Treviso samples are scattered.
steps.quote: there is no homogeneity between the wells of the different sampling sites

steps.action: Compare sample δ2H–δ18O with the GMWL and LMWL and find no substantial deviation, which the authors read as meteoric origin.
steps.quote: do not show a substantial deviation from the Global Meteoric Water Line (GMWL)

steps.action: Resample the same wells in October 2018. Autumn maxima are below 5 TU; Preganziol and Casier are lower in autumn, most Treviso and Quinto wells higher; the spring high-tritium wells remain relatively high.
steps.quote: a second campaign was carried out to evaluate any differences in tritium values in the water collected in the same wells

steps.action: Compare tritium activities with the Italian legal limit of 100 Bq/L; all samples fall well below it.
steps.quote: do not exceed the limits established by the Italian legislation

steps.action: Propose that tritium above rainfall levels comes from external sources (landfill leachate, luminous devices, hospital or laboratory wastewater), against the earlier-noted rival of Arctic/bora snow enrichment.
steps.quote: could be due to external contributions, such as leachate from landfills

steps.action: Compare well tritium with GNIP Locarno March rainfall (5–7 TU) and set 7 TU as the threshold above which contamination is probable.
steps.quote: values higher than 7 denote probable contaminations from surface waters that have interacted with anthropic sources

steps.action: Retain possible leachate-influenced surface-water contamination for the three wells above 7 TU, and conclude that contaminated recharge is low overall.
steps.quote: this could indicate that the recharge of aquifer systems through contaminated surface waters was low

steps.action: Set the findings beside Jasechko et al. (2017), Cook et al. (2018) and Zhao et al. (2018) on young tritiated water reaching fossil aquifers and on groundwater–surface water interaction.
steps.quote: [...] in our case, Jasechko et al. (2017) analyse a [...]

steps.action: Compare with ARPAV water-quality monitoring: 2018 ARPAV data show good quality without anomalies, unlike the differences seen in tritium.
steps.quote: This, of course, is not in line with the data obtained with tritium analyses

steps.action: Attribute chloride and conductivity increases to fossil-water salinization and reject seawater (saline wedge) intrusion, on Na/Cl ratios and trace-metal trends (the latter not shown).
steps.quote: not to the intrusion of the saline wedge, as the Na / Cl is not characteristic of the sea water

steps.action: State two undecided rivals for the low tritium values (long recharge times versus low recharge induced by over-exploitation), and say repeated campaigns are needed to discriminate them.
steps.quote: can allow us to discriminate which of the two hypotheses is realistic

steps.action: Conclude that tritium reveals strong differences in recent-rainwater recharge, reflecting permeability contrasts, and that the aquifer is vulnerable to surface-water contributions and drought-driven salinization.
steps.quote: strong differences in recharge by recent rainwater which reflect the variation in permeability of the gravelly sediments

end.claim: Tritium in 31 artesian wells south of Treviso shows strong spatial differences in recent-rainwater recharge, attributed to permeability contrasts between the gravelly Upper/Middle Plain and the resurgence zone, so the aquifer is vulnerable to surface-water inputs and drought-driven salinization.

decisive_move.sentence: Classifying the enriched-LSC tritium values into recharge-age categories is what turns the measurements into the recharge-variability claim.

gates.evidence: Action: wells were chosen as existing private artesian wells (Table 1 cites an ARPAV 2018 mercury-monitoring report), not by a stated hypothesis. Claim: the seawater-intrusion rival faced a Na/Cl check and the meteoric origin a GMWL comparison, but the headline permeability explanation faced no test it could fail. Registration: the TU class thresholds come from literature and GNIP data, but the paper does not say they were fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Low-level liquid scintillation counting (LKB Quantulus) following ISO 9698
Distillation and electrolytic enrichment of tritium in water samples
Cavity ring-down spectroscopy isotope analyser (Los Gatos LWIA 24-d)

imports.field: nuclear physics / history of weapons testing
imports.item: Bomb-pulse tritium (1952–1963) as a dating marker

limits: No review file was supplied, although the paper states three anonymous referees, so no review sequence is coded. Well selection is not justified; it is inferred from the Table 1 caption that the wells came from an ARPAV mercury-monitoring programme. Four wells (UFE18A05, A11, A16 and one other) have no tritium value, without explanation. Several statements cite evidence that is not shown: trace-metal trends used to reject seawater intrusion, and the claimed chloride and conductivity increase. The LMWL equation is not reported. Precipitation tritium was not measured locally; GNIP Locarno averages stand in for it. Autumn values for the spring high-tritium wells dropped sharply (e.g., UFE18A01 from 7.83 to about 3 TU, Figure 8 (p. 31)), so the 'same trend' is relative and is not reconciled with the age classes. The text is internally inconsistent: 3 wells above 7 TU (§4 ¶5) versus 'only on four samples' (§4 ¶18); 'Figure 2d' refers to Figure 1d. The abstract wrongly calls tritium 'a non-reactive noble gas'. Sub-claim statuses: recharge-age classes estimate_with_resolution (coarse bins, piston-flow assumption acknowledged); leachate contamination in the >7 TU wells best_explanation (tentative; Arctic-snow rival not excluded); seawater intrusion excluded (evidence partly not shown); long recharge versus over-exploitation no_conclusion. The stable-isotope agreement with the meteoric line is presented as consistent with young recharge, but it does not test age and is not coded as a V check. The trace_series composition fits only loosely; the work is largely a descriptive survey with exploratory correlations.

disagreements.support: Tritium shows marked differences between wells where ARPAV chemical monitoring reported good quality without anomalies.
disagreements.quote: This, of course, is not in line with the data obtained with tritium analyses

disagreements.target: Literature use of 'groundwater age' (Suckow 2014; Jasechko 2016; McCallum et al. 2014, 2015; Cartwright et al. 2017)
disagreements.support: The authors note that the term assumes piston flow, which is rarely true, but still use age classes.
disagreements.quote: which is almost never the case in reality

disagreements.target: Clark and Fritz (1997) age of about 50 years for waters below 0.8 TU
disagreements.support: Because of the 1952–1963 bomb peak, the authors extend the age range of the low-tritium class to 50–70 years.
disagreements.quote: it is now possible to detect tritium even in underground waters with residence time in the subsoil of 70 years

disagreements.target: Seawater intrusion linked to over-exploitation as the source of brackish waters (§1 ¶13, Baruffi et al. 2012; Gattacceca et al. [...]
disagreements.support: Na/Cl ratios not characteristic of seawater and trace-metal trends (not shown) point to fossil-water salinization in the studied wells.
disagreements.quote: not to the intrusion of the saline wedge, as the Na / Cl is not characteristic of the sea water

alternatives_considered.reason: Long recharge times could leave tritium below detection for most sampled areas

alternatives_considered.chosen: Age classes based on tritium thresholds (piston-flow reading)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Non-piston, dispersive flow interpretation noted in the cited literature

alternatives_considered.chosen: Values above 7 TU flagged as possible contamination
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Tritium enrichment from Arctic/bora-wind snow carrying stratospheric air
alternatives_considered.reason: Single precipitation events rarely exceed 9 TU and recharge mixing dilutes the signal

alternatives_considered.chosen: Salinization from fossil waters and water-rock interaction
alternatives_considered.reason: Na/Cl not characteristic of seawater; trace-metal trends not correlated with a mixing trend

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Long recharge times versus low recharge in fossil aquifers induced by over-exploitation
alternatives_considered.reason: Data from a single monitoring campaign cannot discriminate between them
